entries.note: The central commitment is a recommendation to consider alternative research approaches.
Marcus quotes his own earlier recommendation and endorses it here.

entries.test: Public studies of harms from webscraping and big-data AI, disaggregated by gender and minority status, would establish whether many disproportionately affect those groups.
entries.note: Disproportionate harm is an empirical claim despite the evaluative wording.

entries.test: Public evaluations showing whether subsequent large language models improved on capabilities measured in June 2022 would test the claimed remaining headroom.
entries.note: He firmly asserts some remaining capacity for improvement without claiming it suffices for AGI.
The substantive claim assigns a 90% probability; it is not an unconditional prediction.
The substantive claim explicitly assigns an 80% probability.

entries.test: The BIG-bench paper's results across model scales, compared with the essay's predictions, would show whether some capabilities improved while others did not as anticipated.
entries.note: The surrounding text makes 'but not at all' an apparent typo for 'but not all.'

entries.test: BIG-bench's published results across model sizes would establish whether the study found progress on some measures but not others.
entries.note: The proposition drops the restriction to the paper's findings and reads as a general statement about scaling.

entries.test: Public architectural descriptions and evaluations of systems achieving the relevant general capabilities would show whether scale alone sufficed or additional approaches were necessary.
entries.note: In context, 'need' asserts a technical necessity for progress beyond scaling, rather than merely a preferred research investment.
The substantive prediction is explicitly hedged as 'not likely.' The separate assertion of agreement can be checked against their public statements.

entries.test: Public documentation and ablation studies of an established AGI system would show whether large-scale symbolic knowledge is crucial to its capabilities.
entries.note: 'Whenever AGI comes' supplies an event-based horizon for the architectural prediction.

entries.test: Public documentation and ablation studies of an established AGI system would show whether explicit cognitive models are crucial to its capabilities.
entries.note: This is Marcus's own prediction, reproduced from his earlier tweet.

entries.test: Public documentation and ablation studies of an established AGI system would show whether operations over variables, including storing, retrieving and comparing values, are crucial to its capabilities.
entries.note: The listed operations give the architectural prediction a concrete empirical interpretation.

entries.test: Public documentation and ablation studies of an established AGI system would show whether an explicit type/token distinction is crucial to its capabilities.
entries.note: The prediction concerns an explicit architectural distinction, not merely similar behavior.
He acknowledges a possible outcome rather than firmly predicting it.

entries.test: Public architectural evidence and capability evaluations of an established AGI system would show whether it requires persistent cognitive models with trustworthy memory storage and retrieval.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion presents these capacities as technical requirements for AGI, rather than a judgment of worth.
The explicit odds below 20% qualify the preceding emphatic 'no way.'

entries.test: Public Comprehension Challenge results and architectural documentation would establish whether a system restricted to CNNs, RNNs and Transformers without writable latent discrete memory can pass.
entries.note: The normalization omits 'latent' from the memory restriction, narrowing the class of systems covered. 'I think … will fail' expresses a firm prediction.
